subject: Recap + prioritized success metrics for Catalyst Health bake-off
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Reed <alex.reed@catalysthealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-02T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap + prioritized success metrics for Catalyst Health bake-off

Hi Alex — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap so we have alignment on next steps and what will move the needle for Catalyst’s evaluation. Happy to adjust if I misunderstood anything.

1) Top pain & goals
- Pain: slow triage for inbound clinical notes (latency spikes at 2k–10k tokens) and high inference cost when running nightly batch summarization.
- Goal: reduce median latency for interactive workflows below 200ms for 256-token responses and drive per-inference cost down ~30% for batch summarization without degrading summary quality.

2) Success metrics you asked us to prioritize
- Latency (P50/P95 token-to-token and end-to-end) for the 256/1024 token profile
- Cost per 1k summarized encounters (nightly batch)
- Semantic parity (>90% on your rubric for clinical fidelity) versus your current vendor
- Operational: warm-start cold-start behavior and KV cache hit rates during peak ingest windows

3) Bake-off scope and timeline
- Redwood will run: interactive latency tests (256/512 tokens), batch summarization run with 10k-document sample, and a parity evaluation using your 100-case clinical rubric.
- Proposed dates: sandbox tests week of Oct 11, live head-to-head smoke tests Oct 18–20.

4) Open questions from today
- Which current model variants (vendor A and vendor B) do you want us to match for quantization/profile parity?
- Is the nightly batch window fixed at 2:00–4:00am ET?
- Any data retention constraints for cache reuse we should be aware of?

5) Next steps (owner)
- Alex/Dana: confirm test dataset and any PII redaction constraints by 10/06 (Dana)
- Camila: share prioritized bake-off matrix and proposed test cases (attached) — by EOD 10/02
- Marissa: schedule engineering deep-dive and baseline collection checklist with your infra team

Attachments: Catalyst_bakeoff_priority_matrix.xlsx (matrix of metrics and weightings), headtohead-test-cases.md (test scripts & sample prompts).

Thanks — will follow up after I get your dataset confirmation.

Best,
Camila
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Catalyst_bakeoff_priority_matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]
From: Alex Reed <alex.reed@catalysthealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dana Lopez <dana.lopez@catalysthealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-02T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + prioritized success metrics for Catalyst Health bake-off

Camila — thanks for the crisp note. This aligns well. Quick clarifications:

- Yes, nightly window is 02:00–04:00 ET and that’s fixed for now.
- For parity targets, please try to match our current vendor baseline (Vendor A) at a 16-bit quantized equivalent; we’ll flag where tradeoffs are acceptable.
- I’ll confirm the dataset and redaction rules by 10/05 — Dana is looping in our security lead for the PII checklist.

Two asks: can Redwood include a short section in the matrix on fallback behavior (how the system degrades when GPUs are saturated) and whether warm/persistent KV cache across jobs is supported? That will be a key tie-breaker for our infra team.

Appreciate it — looking forward to the sandbox run.

—Alex
Head of ML Ops, Catalyst Health
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Reed <alex.reed@catalysthealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-02T18:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + prioritized success metrics for Catalyst Health bake-off

Thanks Alex — noted on the nightly window and Vendor A baseline. Per your asks I updated the matrix to add a small "degradation profile" column and a short note on warm cache semantics; see attachment v2.

Marissa / Avery — flagged for the warm-cache and degrade behavior: Marissa, can you add the technical test we discussed for sustained burst (simulate 2–3x concurrent interactive sessions) and capture failover timings? Avery, please add the economic calc for cost-per-1k-summaries with and without prefix caching.

Low-effort win: if Catalyst can accept a 1–2% drop in semantic parity, Redwood’s 4-bit quantized variant reduces cost per-1k summaries by ~40% in our historical runs. We’ll surface quality diffs in the parity rubric tests so you can decide the trade-off.

Attachment: Catalyst_bakeoff_priority_matrix_v2.xlsx (updated weights + degradation notes).

Camila
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Reed <alex.reed@catalysthealth.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + prioritized success metrics for Catalyst Health bake-off

Alex — looping in the engineering checklist below so you can share with your infra team. Short actionable probes we’ll run in the sandbox:

- Baseline collection: 1000 interactive requests (256 tokens) at 1 RPS to capture cold-start distribution.
- Burst probe: ramp to 50 RPS sustained for 60s, capture queueing/latency and KV hit rates.
- Batch job: run nightly summarization on 10k docs, measure token throughput and per-1k cost.
- Parity eval: our script will run your 100-case rubric and produce a delta table for the three model variants.

We’ll also include a short failover test where we intentionally drop a worker and measure time-to-fallback to a compatible variant (want to show graceful degradation).

Deliverables and timing: checklist + scripts by 10/07; first sandbox run target 10/11.

-Marissa
Principal Solutions Eng | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: headtohead-test-cases.md (text/markdown)]
From: Alex Reed <alex.reed@catalysthealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dana Lopez <dana.lopez@catalysthealth.com>
Date: 2027-10-05T11:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + prioritized success metrics for Catalyst Health bake-off

All — appreciate the rapid turnaround. Dana confirms the dataset and PII redaction rules (see short note below) and we’ll provision a sandbox account for Redwood with a VPN ACL.

Dana L. (Catalyst): Please share the secure link for the sanitized sample when ready; aim for 10/06 so you can hit the 10/11 sandbox start.

Two quick clarifications from our side:
- Can Redwood provide a brief runbook describing how you measure "semantic parity" (metrics and human review process)?
- For the failover test: what does "compatible variant" mean in practice — do you automatically fall back to a smaller model or to a different cluster?

Thanks — will confirm sandbox creds once Dana shares the sample.

—Alex
